title.narrative: Regional Livestock Program in Borana, Ethiopia

description.narrative: Livestock is a key economic engine of arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs) in the Horn of Africa (HOA). Roughly 20 million women and men in Ethiopia, Kenya, and Somalia fully or partially rely on the livestock sector for their livelihood and source of income.Regional Livestock program(RLP )posits that investing in this facilitative approach to market systems development within the livestock sector and the enabling environment will expand existing, and create new, sustainable, climate-smart, economic opportunities in this region and provide the tools for improved household food and nutritional security

Poor women and men are the main beneficiary group of the Regional Livestock Programme. Women and men in this group are reached primarily through support to service providers who in turn provide access to improved and appropriate services and products.

This aims to have vulnerable livestock producers improve the productivity, competitiveness and sustainability when it comes to the production of live animals, milk and other livestock-devoured products with a focus on women and youth.Manage pasture and water resources in an inclusive and sustainable way.Improve herd health and herd management practices .Engage communities in management and mitigation of climate and conflict shocks .
